title: Sunset compatibility-proxy and customer migration safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: We maintain a compatibility-proxy service that transparently translates legacy SDK/endpoints (multiplexed polling, v0-completions, legacy embed batch) to the unified inference API. This layer has accelerated client migrations but now adds operational cost, masks client regressions, and blocks routing optimizations (cost/latency). We need a planned sunsetting of the proxy with strong customer safeguards to avoid breaking production workloads and to reduce long-term maintenance and SLA surface area.

Goal: Deliver a migration playbook, automation, telemetry gates, SDK adapters, enterprise carve-outs, and a staged timeline to retire the compatibility-proxy with minimal customer disruption. This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout milestones for the proxy sunset.

Out of scope: Internal refactor of runtime routing kernels, wholesale SDK language rewrites (these will be separate engineering tickets), and any model alias changes unrelated to proxy behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide published in Console docs with per-endpoint mappings and example request/response transforms
SDK adapter (JS + Python) released: opt-in compatibility shim that logs deprecation telemetry and offers automatic field mapping; tests show parity for 95% of observed traffic patterns
Telemetry gates defined and implemented: proxy usage by customer, error-rate delta, and latency delta metrics instrumented and visible in Console (token-level and route-level)
Customer communications plan agreed and executed: early notice to top 200 customers (90 days), in-console banners for active users, and staged email cadence
Canary sunset executed for non-production customers: 30-day shadow window with automated rollback criteria defined
Enterprise exceptions workflow documented: process, SLA adjustments, legal/contract signoff template
Rollback and mitigation automations available: temporary auto-reenable of proxy per-customer via support playbook and console toggle within 15 minutes
All dependent product tickets and engineering change requests are linked and owners assigned
Security review completed for adapter code and migration tooling (KMS access or secrets handling if required)
plan: Phase 0 (Discovery, now - 2026-03-31): Collect usage telemetry, inventory endpoints routed through proxy, and produce migration impact matrix by customer and by endpoint
Phase 1 (Guides & Tooling, 2026-04-01 - 2026-05-15): Publish migration docs; release OSS SDK adapters (opt-in); create a console migration checklist and per-route compatibility reports
Phase 2 (Canary & Telemetry, 2026-05-16 - 2026-05-31): Enable canary sunset for internal/test tenants and low-risk customers; ensure telemetry gates report and alert; iterate on adapter fixes

Phase 3 (Gradual Sunset, 2026-06-01 - 2026-07-31): Start ramped shutdown by customer cohort (non-paying/dev -> mid-tier -> enterprise exceptions), enforce provider quotas and rate limits; provide direct support for migration handoff
Phase 4 (Finish & Audit, 2026-08-01 - 2026-08-15): Complete removal from routing, run audit, update all docs, and close dependent tickets
rollout_timeline: 90-day announcement to all customers once Phase 1 publish is complete
60-day targeted outreach to high-usage customers with migration risk score >= medium
30-day in-console banners and opt-in test window for customers to validate traffic against adapters
D-Day: begin cohort 1 shutdown for developer tiers; monitor telemetry gates for 72 hours before proceeding
Follow-up cohorts every 2 weeks with preflight telemetry validation
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: High-volume customers see unexpected response delta -> Mitigation: Provide shadowing and request/response diff tooling; hold canary for that customer and assign SE
Risk: Adapter parity gaps cause functional regressions -> Mitigation: Maintain hotfix channel, additional test harnesses, and automated synthetic tests based on captured production traces
Risk: Customers on private/offline deployments can't accept change -> Mitigation: Offer extended enterprise exception with contractual timeline and security review
Risk: Telemetry doesn't surface critical regressions quickly -> Mitigation: Instrument alerting thresholds and a daily migration health digest to product/eng/support
stakeholder_review: Product: Aisha Patel - signoff on migration strategy
Engineering: Priya Rao (runtime) - validate feasibility of per-route toggles
Console: Leo Martinez - confirm in-console banner and per-customer report UX
Legal: Cynthia Alvarez - review enterprise exception templates
Support & CS: Nora Singh - prepare runbook and escalation matrix
notes:
Scope adjustments from initial discovery: we decided not to auto-migrate customer credentials or rewrite client SDK network stack — adapters will operate at request/response transform layer only. Engineering owners requested an extra 2-week buffer for adapter integration tests. Support will create a prioritized queue for customers flagged as high-risk by the migration impact matrix.

Follow-ups: Create ENG tickets for adapter performance profiling, DES ticket for migration UX mocks, and schedule a cross-functional migration readiness review the week before Phase 2.
